title: ephemeral-circuit-quarantine-and-prioritized-reservation-guard
author: Priya Shah
description: Context: We observed several customer incidents where transient regional load spikes caused sticky circuit state and long-lived inflight queues for multi-tenant routes. Root cause: connection stalls + aggressive kv-drain heuristics interacting with tenant-weighted admission causing some tenants to remain dormant while others monopolized inflight reservation slots. Motivation: reduce blast radius of sticky circuits and provide a short-term prioritized reservation path for critical tenants to avoid prolonged hard quarantine during region instability. Goals: 1) Add an ephemeral 'circuit quarantine' state that temporarily isolates circuits flagged as high stall-risk and drains inflight safely; 2) Add a prioritized reservation bucket (time-limited) to allow small-quantity critical requests to bypass soft-quarantine and validate recovery; 3) Ensure telemetry and debug hooks for post-mortem (per-tenant circuit timeline + tokenized drain traces). Design summary: - Introduced a transient circuit state TRANSIENT_QUARANTINE with a short TTL (configurable, default 30s) that isolates the failing circuit from normal routing but continues to accept low-priority probes and health rechecks. - Implemented a prioritized_reservation slot allocator: shards maintain N prioritized slots per epoch (configurable by tenant tier). Requests tagged with priority:critical may acquire a reservation if available; reservations have a strict max tokens/call and are rate-limited to avoid starving background drains. - Modified admission controller to favor prioritized reservations over ordinary warmup paths while still observing global latency SLO budgets. - Added heuristics to avoid circuit stickiness: when a circuit transitions to TRANSIENT_QUARANTINE we set a soft-reopen backoff that grows exponentially per re-open attempt but imposes an upper bound to avoid permanent blackholing. - Telemetry: emit circuit_quarantine.{enter,exit,reopen_attempt} counters, per-tenant prioritized_reservation.granted/denied gauges, and structured traces that include kv-cache sizes and drain progress at transition boundaries. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless tenant is opted into prioritized reservations via account tier or config flag. Checklist: - [x] Spec and design doc in Linear (ENG-842) - [x] Unit tests for reservation allocator and TTL transitions - [x] Integration test: simulated regional stall scenario - [x] Telemetry included and wired to Console dashboards - [x] Feature flag gated rollout plan - [x] Docs update for SLO guidance (docs/observability/quarantine.md) Commits (summary): - Add TRANSIENT_QUARANTINE state machine and state transitions (Priya Shah) - Implement prioritized_reservation allocator with per-epoch accounting (Priya Shah) - Admission controller: prioritize reservations & enforce token caps (Ben Turner) - Telemetry: counters/gauges + trace annotations (Aisha Khan) - Tests: unit + integration + flake fixes (Miguel Ortega) Files changed (high-level): - runtime/circuit/state_machine.go (new states + transitions) - runtime/admission/prioritized_reservation.go (allocator) - runtime/admission/allocator_test.go (unit tests) - serving/probes/quarantine_probe.go (probe and health checks) - observability/metrics/registry.go (new metric defs) - console/dashboards/quarantine-overview.json (dashboard) - docs/observability/quarantine.md (documentation) - sdk/python/examples/prioritized_reservation_example.py (example usage) Testing & CI: - Local integration harness: simulated region egress stall, verified TRANSIENT_QUARANTINE TTL respected and prioritized reservations allowed 25 requests/min for smoke tenants. - Load test: 10k concurrent tenants, prioritized reservations did not increase 95th percentile latency by >1.2% for main region under test. - CI: unit and integration suites passed on first run; flakiness fix for allocator test added in second commit. Review conversation (high level): - Miguel: "Please add an additional guard to ensure reservation tokens can't be hoarded by a single connection; otherwise LGTM." - Priya: "Added per-connection cap (tokens_per_connection) and a unit test covering edge case." - Aisha: "Would like a clearer rollback path in rollout plan; add a safety kill-switch via feature-flag and an immediate metric alarm." - Priya: "Added feature-flag bypass and an alert rule tied to circuit_quarantine.enter spike rate; described in rollout section." - Ben: "Telemetry looks good; can we annotate traces with tenant tier?" - Priya: "Done, traces now include tenant_tier metadata." Approvals: - Aisha Khan: approved - Miguel Ortega: approved - Ben Turner: approved CI checks: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - lint: pass - e2e: pass Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable feature-flag in staging + 2 small production clusters with monitoring enabled (24h). - Stage 2 (tiered rollout): enable prioritized reservations for tier:critical customers only for 72h, monitor circuit_quarantine.enter rate and P95 latency. - Stage 3: toggle on for tier:standard with conservative slot counts and an automatic auto-off if circuit_quarantine.enter increases > 3x baseline within 1h. - Rollback: disable feature-flag (instant) and publish patch to revert state transitions if necessary. Post-merge tasks: - Add a Console runbook entry and a Linear follow-up for quota tuning (ENG-872). - Engage SRE on daily checks for first 72h. Related incidents / why-hotfix: SUP-1198 documented a production outage where several tenants experienced extended cold starts after a short regional egress throttling event. This change aims to reduce repeat incidents by avoiding sticky negative circuit state and giving critical tenants a fast-path to remain responsive. Merge: squashed and merged via merge commit (SHA: ab12cd34ef56). Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the prioritized reservation small and rate-limited to reduce potential SLO regressions; we will iterate on sizing after initial telemetry. Documentation and Console dashboard updated as part of the change.
